page: Google Cloud Platform e2-micro is a shared-core virtual machine belonging to the E2 instance family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to a single physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads, operating at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU allocation is shared, specifically utilizing 1/8 of a physical core. It is configured with 1.0 GB of system memory, providing 0.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations place the e2-micro in the bottom 10% across all tested performance categories. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 132.9, and the multi-core score is 171.0. Memory bandwidth is highly constrained, showing 9.73 GB/sec for small-block cached reads, which drops to 0.1 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads, alongside a write speed of 1.33 GB/sec. Passmark metrics reflect this profile, with a CPU score of 201.56 and a database operations score of 57.19. Static web serving throughput is measured at 0.17 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-micro is designed as a budget-friendly tier for workloads with minimal resource demands. The shared-core architecture allows for low-cost baseline operations but introduces performance trade-offs under sustained utilization. This instance is suited for lightweight utility tasks, basic microservices, development testing, or simple static web serving where high throughput and low latency are not critical.
